ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended, especially Articles 5-2 through 5-6 on customer due diligence and beneficial ownership); Financial Transactions Reports Act (Act No. 7606, as amended); Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality (Act No. 5493, as amended); Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 10000, as amended); Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (Act No. 8820, as amended); Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Presidential Decree No. 20019, as amended). The Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), acting within the Financial Services Commission, is the competent AML/CFT supervisor and maintains non-public beneficial ownership and transaction information.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Corporate Registration Certificate) for the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (District Court Registry Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel authentication paths only; do not chain. Hague Apostille Path: notarized registration exemplification from the Korean registry then obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea, accepted directly by all Apostille Convention member states. Consular Legalization Path: for non-member destination states, notarized Korean excerpt then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication then legalization by the consulate of the destination state in Seoul.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Corporate Registry Extract and National Tax Service Business Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office and National Tax Service (NTS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel authentication paths only; do not chain. Hague Apostille Path: certified registry extract and NTS certificate then apostillization via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; no consular legalization. Consular Legalization Path: certified Korean documents then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication then destination-state consular legalization; each path is mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Pre-Incorporation, Name Clearance and Trust Escrow Account Opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public for Korean-executed documents; competent authority of the parent jurisdiction for foreign-executed powers of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel authentication paths only; do not chain. Hague Apostille Path: notarized resolution/PoA executed in the Republic of Korea or an Apostille member state then Apostille from the state of execution; no consular legalization. Consular Legalization Path: notarized resolution/PoA then authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the state of execution then legalization by the Korean consulate in that state, or Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication then destination-state consular legalization if the document is Korean-origin.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Yuhan Hoesa Limited Liability Company Charter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office for certified registered copy; signed by all incorporators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel authentication paths only; do not chain. Hague Apostille Path: certified true copy from the Korean court registry or notarized original then Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; no consular legalization. Consular Legalization Path: certified true copy from the registry then Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication then destination-state consular legalization; never combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the SPAC Trust/Escrow Account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed bank or foreign bank KYC/compliance department in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel authentication paths only; do not chain. Hague Apostille Path: original bank reference letter with notarized branch manager signature then Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing bank's home state; no consular legalization. Consular Legalization Path: notarized bank reference letter then authentication by the issuing state's foreign ministry then legalization by the Korean consulate in that state; paths are mutually exclusive and sequential combining is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Beneficial Ownership Declaration and Organizational Chart reflecting all 25% or higher UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and legal representative of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel authentication paths only; do not chain. Hague Apostille Path: notarized declaration in the Republic of Korea then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille; accepted directly in apostille states. Consular Legalization Path: notarized declaration then Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication then legalization by the consulate of the destination non-member state in Seoul; both paths are mutually exclusive alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All prospective directors, shareholders, beneficiaries, escrow counterparties, authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners must be screened in real time and continuously against the UN Security Council Consolidated List; the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List and all OFAC sanctions programs; the U.S. BIS Denied Persons and Entity Lists; the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's restricted persons register and domestic terrorist financing designations. Screening must use fuzzy matching, exact passport and ID numbers, date-of-birth, address, nickname, Hangul, Chinese-character and Latin-script name variants, plus adverse-media review. Any PEP, including immediate family members and close associates, automatically triggers enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and heightened transaction monitoring for at least 12 months after PEP status ceases. Suspicious transactions must be reported to KoFIU as required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea, iros.go.kr, and the commercial registry of the competent district court registry office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in the Korean legal form designation Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), with the company's distinctive name element rendered in Hangul transliteration or, where accepted by the registry, a Latin-script trade name. The statutory naming doctrine requires a four-tier convention: (1) a distinctive element that is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or famous trademark; (2) an industry or business objective indicator; (3) the Korean legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and (4) no prohibited or sensitive token without prior approval from the Financial Services Commission or relevant ministry. The English/foreign name may be used as an auxiliary trade name but the Han-gul-registered name is controlling for legal service and court filing purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When a name registration is rejected, the applicant must within 14 days of the rejection decision file a written objection with the head of the district court registry setting out the corrected name, documentary evidence of prior trademark and company name search, and, where applicable, the Financial Services Commission approval for the SPAC designation. If the registry confirms the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within one week of written notice. The appeal must attach the rejection certificate, proposed Articles of Association, UBO details, and ministerial consents. A further appeal to the Supreme Court of Korea is available only on a question of law. During the pending appeal, a stay order should be requested to prevent the name from being registered by another applicant.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Yuhan Hoesa whose principal business is an ISIC 6499 blank-check entity for public market acquisition mergers (SPAC), a virtual office or commercial mailbox is materially rejected by the Korean National Tax Service, Korean banks, the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Exchange. The Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act requires the SPAC issuer to maintain a physical head office in the Republic of Korea where board meetings are held, books and records are kept, internal controls are administered, and the trust escrow account documentation is retained. A registered agent address alone does not satisfy commercial substance and will trigger enhanced due diligence, likely bank account denial, and a high probability of licensing rejection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) NTS unannounced on-site inspection of the registered office in the first year: 35% probability for a newly incorporated LLC, rising to 70% where a SPAC license is pending; (ii) FSC/FSS supervisory on-site inspection after SPAC listing: 60% baseline, exceeding 85% if suspicious transaction reports have been filed; (iii) court registry bailiff address verification at registration: 20%; (iv) bank KYC field visit before trust escrow release: 55%. Quantified overall risk for this SPAC vehicle is high, with a 70-80% estimated probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months after incorporation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 543 through 613 (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company), in particular Articles 543, 546, 548, 550, 553, 555, 560 and 561; for the Special Purpose Acquisition Company (SPAC) activity, Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, Articles 77(3), 80, 119 and 120; Korea Exchange KOSDAQ Listing Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: District Court Registration Office of the Seoul Central District Court, or the District Court Registration Office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, under the supervision of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation of the Yuhan Hoesa together with the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company under the Commercial Registration Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act; however, for an ISIC 6499 SPAC listing vehicle, at least KRW 3,000,000,000 (approximately USD 2,300,000) must be raised by public offering, and 90% of the gross offering proceeds must be placed into a qualified trust/escrow account maintained at a Korean bank, with withdrawal restricted to permitted expenses, redemption payments, or consummation of a qualifying business combination.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the duly convened board of directors of the undersigned Yuhan Hoesa (the Company), acting under Article 561 of the Korean Commercial Act and the Company’s articles of incorporation, hereby ratifies, approves, and adopts the executed Articles of Incorporation, including the business purpose of acting exclusively as a special purpose acquisition company for the acquisition of a target enterprise and the raising of capital through a public offering, such business purpose to remain within ISIC 6499.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the authorized share capital of the Company is fixed at the amount set forth in the subscription ledger and divided into registered and reporting shares of equal par value; each founding member has subscribed to the shares opposite their name and the full subscription price has been unconditionally deposited into a dedicated capital escrow account opened with a commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, from which funds shall not be withdrawn except to pay permitted formation expenses, satisfy redemption requests, or close a qualifying business combination approved by the board and disclosed to shareholders.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be at [address to be inserted in Metro Seoul jurisdiction], Korea, and the Company authorizes its officers to execute a lease and register such address as the statutory seat, with the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office acting as the registry.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [bank name] is appointed and authorized as the bank of the Company; the Chief Executive Officer, together with any one director, are jointly authorized to open, operate, close, and sign on deposit, trust escrow, and SWIFT wire accounts, and to issue all payment instructions for capital redemption or merger consideration.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following natural persons are elected to the statutory offices of the Company: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer; [Name] as Compliance Officer; and [Name] as Company Secretary, with all such officers empowered to sign securities filings, listing applications, banking mandates, and registration forms before the Financial Services Commission, Korea Exchange, National Tax Service, and Court Registry.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Compliance Officer shall establish anti-money-laundering policies, maintain a trust account ledger, cause the preparation of separate bookkeeping for corporate assets and the escrow assets, and file all disclosures required of a SPAC; all directors shall act in a strictly fiduciary manner and no business other than the SPAC purpose shall be carried on.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name and Capital Structure Certification, Escrow Opening, and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (www.iros.go.kr); local Korean notary public; commercial bank authorised by the Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a capacity and eligibility review on the internet registration system of the Supreme Court for the proposed Korean name of the Yuhan Hoesa. Prepare and notarize the Articles of Incorporation before a Korean notary public, ensure that the names and subscription amounts of the founding members are included, and open a dedicated escrow account at a Korean commercial bank for the SPAC trust funds. Because the Company is incorporated as a blank-check vehicle under ISIC 6499, use a capital subscription account instead of a general current account in order to preserve traceability of the share capital deposit and the later IPO proceeds. The incorporators must sign the Articles of Incorporation in duplicate, affix their seals or use notarized signatures, and confirm that the business purpose limits activities to registration, public offering, merger search, and related fiduciary functions.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Notarized certified copy of each incorporator's passport or Korean residence registration certificate
Capital contribution trust/escrow agreement
Written consent for the registered office address
Subscription ledger showing names and share subscriptions
Power of attorney if execution is delegated
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search fails or the notary issues a query, submit an alternative company name, amend the Articles of Incorporation accordingly, and re-notarize the document; the remedy normally adds two business days to the SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, Commercial Registration Division, or the District Court Registration Office for the jurisdiction of the principal office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the competent District Court Registration Office together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital payment certificate issued by the bank, the specimen of the corporate seal, and proof of payment of registration tax and education surcharge. The court will accept the application only if the statutory incorporators or their authorized agents appear at the registration counter and execute the registration form. After successful examination, the registry assigns a corporate registration number and issues the certified corporate registration extract, which constitutes conclusive evidence of legal existence of the Yuhan Hoesa. This step is complete when the company comes into existence as a separate juridical person under Korean law.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company
Capital payment certificate issued by the bank
Specimen of corporate seal and individual officer seals
Proof of registration tax payment
Identity documents of directors, incorporators, and appointed officers
First board resolution approving directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a suspension or correction notice, cure the immaterial defects within the statutory correction period by filing amended documents and pay any deficient fee; if the application is rejected, a new application may be filed after the defect is cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Office Business Registration and Corporate Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), local District Tax Office Business Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after incorporation registration, file a business-start registration with the National Tax Service through the local District Tax Office. Submit the certified corporate registration extract, Articles of Incorporation, corporate seal certificate, lease agreement or ownership evidence for the registered office, and identification of all statutory officers. The NTS will verify the corporate existence, registered address, and intended ISIC 6499 classification before issuing the corporate taxpayer business registration certificate. After the certificate is issued, the company may activate fully operational bank accounts, open the SPAC trust escrow account, and begin legally issuing invoices or maintaining financial books; all foreign shareholders or foreign officers must present certified translations and foreign registration records.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form
Certified copy of corporate registration extract
Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate
Lease agreement or ownership evidence for the registered office
Identification and alien registration records of foreign officers or shareholders
Bank account nomination form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS suspends the application due to defective address or officer records, file corrected documentation within five business days; if the tax office conducts an office field visit, provide the lease, corporate records, and signed occupancy consent to expedite issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SPAC Financial Authorization, KOSDAQ Listing Review, and Post-Listing Compliance Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC), Securities Disclosure and Equity Market Division; Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) DART electronic disclosure system; Korea Exchange Inc. (KRX) KOSDAQ Market Headquarters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After corporate and business registration are effective, submit the SPAC listing application to the Korea Exchange for preliminary KOSDAQ review and file the securities registration statement with the FSC through the DART electronic disclosure system under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act. The FSC will review the registration statement, the underwriter agreement, the trustee or escrow arrangement, the corporate governance charter, and the conflict-of-interest policy. The registration statement becomes effective on the date designated by the FSC after any requested amendments are accepted, and the KRX grants listing approval only after verifying the minimum offering size, the 90% escrow trust requirement, the redemption rights of shareholders, and the compliance officer appointment. Once approved, the company must maintain periodic disclosure, AML surveillance, and continuous SPAC reporting obligations before trading begins.
required_dossiers: KRX KOSDAQ preliminary listing application
Securities registration statement prepared on DART
Financial statements audited by a Korean licensed accounting firm
Underwriting agreement with a licensed securities company
Trust escrow or contractual contingent capital agreement
Corporate governance charter and conflict-of-interest policy
Anti-money-laundering policy and compliance officer appointment resolution
Legal opinion on SPAC suitability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC issues a request for amendment or the KRX issues a deficiency letter, respond in writing within the stated correction period, ordinarily 30 days; after curing the deficiencies, re-file the amended registration statement or listing application and await a new effective date or review panel decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Korea Exchange (KRX) for SPAC financial authorization; Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and local EIA agencies are Not Applicable for pure office-based SPAC activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Effectiveness of Securities Registration Statement under Articles 119-120 of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act and KRX KOSDAQ Listing Approval for the SPAC; industrial operation license: Not Applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Korea Environment Corporation) - Not Applicable for this office-only entity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity under ISIC 6499; no EIA registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: 0 kg/year VOC emissions; 0 m3/day wastewater discharge; no hazardous chemical storage; therefore all quantitative discharge thresholds under the Clean Air Conservation Act and Water Environment Conservation Act are not triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable at formation stage except that the registered office lease must satisfy basic fire safety compliance under the Fire Prevention, Installation and Maintenance Act and general office occupational health standards under the Occupational Safety and Health Act; no civil defense operational clearance is required for SPAC activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity with a domestic place of business in Korea: (1) register the foreign company's Korean branch/domestic place of business with the relevant Commercial Court registry and obtain the Foreign Company Domestic Place of Business Registration Certificate; (2) within 20 days of actual commencement of taxable business, file the statutory Application for Business Registration with the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over the Korean place of business, using HomeTax or in-person counter service; attach the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, evidence of the Korean place of business, representative identity documents, and a power of attorney if represented by a tax agent; (3) the NTS will issue the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves simultaneously as the Corporate Tax TIN, the VAT registration ID, and the withholding-tax registration identifier; (4) for a foreign entity with no fixed Korean place of business that nonetheless has Korean-source tax obligations, the NTS may assign a withholding/corporate taxpayer number through HomeTax, but a Business Registration Number is still mandatory before making any domestic taxable supply or claiming export zero-rating.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or an elective hybrid-mismatch classification. A Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily taxable at entity level on its worldwide income under the Corporate Tax Act. The only available group-level mechanism is the statutory consolidated corporate tax filing for qualifying Korean parent-subsidiary groups, which is not a pass-through or hybrid-mismatch election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary registration threshold; VAT registration is mandatory for any person who commences a taxable business in Korea, regardless of turnover, and must be completed within 20 days of business commencement. A simplified taxable person filing threshold applies at KRW 80,000,000 of annual taxable supplies, but that threshold does not relieve a business from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT payers must issue tax invoices. Electronic tax invoices must be generated through the NTS HomeTax electronic tax invoice system or an NTS-certified ERP/API integrator and transmitted to the NTS at issuance; the NTS maintains a centralized transaction-clearance database. There is no separate physical digital stamp; anti-fraud controls include automatic cross-matching of electronic tax invoices against customs export declarations, mandatory cash receipts for qualifying B2C sales, and real-time audit flags for unmatched or irregular invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, the 0% export rate is available where: (i) goods are exported to a foreign country and the export is evidenced by a customs export declaration; (ii) services are supplied to a person located outside Korea and the service is actually performed, used, or consumed outside Korea; or (iii) the supply is international maritime or air transportation. For a SPAC entity, issuance of shares or securities is not a taxable supply; any cross-border financial or advisory services may be zero-rated only if the place of supply is outside Korea and the recipient is a non-resident, supported by contemporaneous service-use documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (statutory export declaration lodged via Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS)
Bill of Lading (original or electronic ocean bill of lading) or Air Waybill
Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation / Inward Remittance Certificate (bank-to-bank SWIFT credit evidence for repatriated export proceeds)
Export Contract or Purchase Order evidencing the cross-border sale to the foreign counterparty
Service-consumption dossier for qualifying cross-border services, evidencing offshore place of supply and actual use by the non-resident recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Substantiation is scrutinized through triangulation of HomeTax zero-rated VAT returns, Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations, and foreign exchange bank settlement records. If the 0% export claim is not supported or export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory settlement period, the NTS reverses the zero-rating, assesses VAT at 10% on the export selling price, and imposes additional taxes under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including additional tax for underreporting (generally 10% for non-fraudulent underreporting and 40% for fraudulent or unlawful underreporting), daily late-payment interest, and withdrawal or clawback of any prior refund. Intentional evasion also carries criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and may extend the statutory assessment window for retrospective correction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won (KRW) operates under a managed floating exchange rate regime with liberalized current account and capital account transactions, but significant verification and reporting obligations remain in force. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree require that all cross-border settlements be routed through authorized foreign exchange banks, with transaction-level purpose codes and supporting documentation. For a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) structured as a Yuhan Hoesa, the capital account liberalization allows inbound equity injections, but the initial share subscription proceeds and subsequent trust/escrow funding must be accompanied by a certificate of foreign investment registration, capital contribution receipt, and business plan validation when remitting into a designated capital escrow account. Current account transactions, including dividends and liquidation proceeds, are freely repatriable after corporate tax withholding, but profit remittances require audited financial statements and tax clearance certificates from the National Tax Service (NTS). The Korean authorities do not impose a mandatory surrender of export proceeds, yet all non-KRW receipts must be reported to the reporting bank within 30 days of receipt, and exporters must either retain the foreign currency in a domestic foreign currency account or convert to KRW within the statutory settlement timeline. Derivatives and hedging instruments are permitted for trade and debt servicing purposes, but speculative FX transactions by non-financial entities require prior approval under the soundness guidelines. Overall, the KRW is convertible for bona fide business operations, but administrative compliance and documentary evidence burdens create material friction for SPAC treasury management, particularly for ring-fenced acquisition funds.

stage_4.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: According to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information Reporting Regulations, all export proceeds must be collected through an authorized foreign exchange bank within one year from the date of export shipment, unless an extension is granted by the bank for justified reasons such as long-term receivables or construction projects. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; an exporter may retain the full amount of foreign currency in a designated foreign currency deposit account or convert to KRW at the prevailing market rate. However, the exporter must report the receipt of export proceeds to the reporting bank within 30 calendar days of collection, using the prescribed export proceeds receipt report form. Failure to adhere to the one-year collection timeline triggers a penalty and may affect customs clearance for subsequent shipments. For a SPAC entity, this surrender rule is relevant only for incidental operating income, as the core treasury inflows are capital contributions and trust distributions, which are classified under capital account transactions and subject to separate investment registration and reporting procedures under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border fintech EMIs present low viability for a South Korean Yuhan Hoesa SPAC. The Banking Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act grant deposit-taking and foreign exchange brokerage authority exclusively to licensed banks and authorized foreign exchange institutions. An offshore digital EMI without a Korean banking license cannot operate settlement accounts, issue local IBANs, or process KRW clearing. Although certain fintech companies offer multi-currency wallets, they act as resellers of banking infrastructure and require a domestic banking partner for each transaction, adding counterparty risk and compliance opacity. The Financial Services Commission (FSC) prohibits unlicensed providers from undertaking foreign exchange purchase and sale notifications, which are mandatory for every inbound and outbound cross-border transfer. Therefore, the treasury blueprint must rely exclusively on Tier-1 commercial banks with full foreign exchange dealing licenses, global trading platforms, and established capability to service blank-check acquisition vehicles. Any alternative payment institution must obtain a registered foreign exchange business license under Article 8 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, a process that is operationally prohibitive for a newly formed SPAC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident corporate entity and its statutory directors, Korean banks ordinarily mandate a physical bank visit by at least one authorized signatory director and the gatekeeper of the ultimate beneficial owner, presenting an original certificate of incorporation, company seal, articles of incorporation, and passport. Remote consular proxy opening is not a universal right: banks may accept a notarized power of attorney authenticated by the Korean consulate or an apostille under the Hague Convention, but such acceptance is discretionary and requires the proxy to be a Korean-licensed attorney or a locally resident officer of a registered accounting firm. In practice, major banks like Shinhan and Hana permit hybrid remote KYC via video interview for clients introduced by a top-tier global correspondent bank, yet statutory directors must still physically appear at a Korean branch or at a Korean diplomatic mission to verify identity. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) guidance and the Financial Services Commission's Prevention of Money Laundering Regulations require face-to-face identification for high-risk corporate vehicles such as SPACs. Therefore, the blueprint mandates at least one physical visit by the chief executive officer or a designated founding shareholder, with a documented KYC interview covering the intended acquisition sectors, the trust release triggers, and the ultimate beneficiary identity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained capitalization structure with non-resident minority investors holding significant equity without clear operating track record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A fully sourced equity contribution ledger, bank statements of each contributing investor for the last 9 months, a notarized declaration of source of wealth, and an audited statement from the founding shareholder's home jurisdiction confirming the origin of funds. For corporate shareholders, provide financial statements for the last 3 years, certificate of good standing, and a corporate ownership chain chart up to the ultimate human beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SPAC's escrow arrangement with a foreign trustee and planned future public listing raises concerns about abuse of the trust account for money laundering or tax evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A legal opinion from a Korean law firm confirming the escrow agreement complies with the CapTable under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, a copy of the trust deed with the licensed Korean escrow agent, and a written commitment to submit quarterly escrow statements to the bank. Also, provide the prospectus or preliminary offering circular under preparation and the exchange listing plan for the Korean Exchange (KRX) or a recognized overseas exchange.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure of the target acquisition targets or beneficial owners connected to jurisdictions subject to FATF or Korean government warnings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A due diligence report identifying each target's ultimate beneficial owner, sanctions screening results from reputable databases (World-Check, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance), and a transaction rationale memorandum detailing the commercial purpose. Provide certificates of tax residence for all involved parties and a written confirmation that no target operates in FATF high-risk jurisdictions, or if it does, a comprehensive enhanced due diligence package including local government approvals and an independent audit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border wire flows from and to unusual intermediary accounts prior to the SPAC public offering, which may appear as structured layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A five-year cash-flow projection for the escrow period, a list of expected counterparties with legal identification, and a notarized board resolution authorizing the treasury officer to execute transfers. Include the foreign investment registration certificate (under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act) for each inbound capital injection, and a standard bank trajectory where funds flow directly from the investing bank account to the designated escrow account without third-party pass-through.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the SPAC must first be registered with the Korean government via the Foreign Investment Promotion Act by filing a foreign investment report with a domestic bank or the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA). After receiving the foreign investment registration certificate (IRC), capital can be remitted through SWIFT MT103 messages with the purpose code '7120' (equity subscription) or '7810' (other foreign direct investment), referencing the IRC number. The receiving bank will verify the IRC, confirm the exchange rate margin, and issue a certificate of foreign investment capital receipt, which is mandatory for capital verification (proof of paid-in capital) for corporate registration. All funds must be settled through the Korea Communication Settlement System (BOK-Wire+) to the designated capital escrow account. The bank will apply a standard T+1 value date, and any KRW conversion of foreign currency capital must be executed at the interbank market rate with a bank spread capped under the Foreign Exchange Regulations. The capital verification report must be filed with the court registry within two weeks of receipt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements related to future acquisitions and operating expenses, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 via the corporate banking platform, using the bank's electronic file transfer (EFTS) requesting the appropriate foreign exchange purpose code (e.g., '6220' for professional and business services, '7130' for offshore investment, or '7110' for acquisition of securities). Documentary collections (D/P, D/A) are permissible for import trade purchases, while commercial letters of credit are advised for high-value acquisitions to mitigate counterparty risk. Korean banks require all outbound disbursements above USD 50,000 to be supported by an underlying contract, invoice, or board resolution; for the SPAC, the trustee's disbursement instruction and the escrow release certificate must accompany the payment order. The BOK-Wire+ rail is used for domestic KRW transfers; for cross-border, the bank will route via its global network (e.g., Shinhan's SWIFT relationship, Woori's international clearing) ensuring IRU (international relay unit) settlement. All outbound wires are subject to real-time screening against OFAC, EU, and Korean sanctions lists, and the bank retains the right to request additional beneficial ownership data for third-country payees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward contracts (FX forwards) up to 24 months, permitted only against a genuine trade or transaction exposure and subject to the bank's credit facility and underlying documentation requirement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in KRW are prohibited onshore for domestic entities; only offshore non-resident counterparties may enter into KRW NDFs, and domestic SPACs cannot use NDFs without prior special approval from the foreign exchange authorities

Cross-currency swap contracts (CIR) for converting USD capital to KRW with a fixed exchange rate and swap points, allowed for capital account obligations with prior approval from the MOEF for amounts exceeding USD 10 million

Covered interest arbitrage swaps with a Korean bank's overseas branch, permissible if the swap is used to hedge the SPAC's acquisition currency exposure and the bank files the foreign exchange derivative position report to the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending December 31, file no later than March 31 of the following year; for a non-December fiscal year-end, file within 3 months from the fiscal year-end date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If filed late or omitted, additional tax (negligent penalty) of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax is imposed; if the tax base was under-reported, a 10%-20% under-report penalty applies; unpaid tax accrues daily delinquency interest at the statutory rate (approximately 0.025% per day); persistent non-filing after demand can trigger NTS forced collection, seizure of bank accounts/assets, and cancellation of the business registration. Penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes and Corporate Tax Act may also subject directors and managers to personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surtax Return (Local Corporate Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Metropolitan or local government (Si/Gun/Gu) of the tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending December 31, file no later than April 30 of the following year; for other fiscal years, within 4 months from the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underpayment triggers a 20% negligent additional tax on the unpaid local income tax and daily overdue interest; prolonged non-payment can be collected through compulsory local tax execution, business closure order, or administrative cancellation of the relevant business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report (Annual Securities Report) for SPAC under the Capital Markets Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART; simultaneously notified to Korea Exchange (KRX)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 SPAC, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing subjects the company to a regulatory corrective order, fines up to KRW 500 million under the Capital Markets Act for serious violations, suspension of securities listing, and ultimately administrative delisting by KRX if the filing is not cured within the KRX grace period (typically 10 business days). A false or omitted material statement may additionally create criminal liability and civil damages exposure to directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements for statutory external audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service and Korea Exchange for listed SPAC; submitted to members at the annual meeting and filed through DART with the annual business report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a listed SPAC, audit report must accompany the annual business report within 90 days after fiscal year-end; for a private Yuhan Hoesa above the audit threshold, audited financial statements must be prepared and submitted to members' approval within 6 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a certified audit may result in FSS designation of a supervising auditor, imposition of administrative sanctions, a penalty related to audit fees, removal of listing eligibility, and criminal fines for obstruction of audit. For an audited private company, the tax authority may deny deductions and assess negligence penalties if unaudited statements are used for tax bases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Meeting of Members and Filing of Changes to the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (District Court registry having jurisdiction); members approve annual financial statements and any changes in managers or registered matters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending December 31, the members' meeting and financial statement approval must be completed within 6 months after fiscal year-end; any resulting amendment in registered particulars in the Commercial Register must be filed within 2 weeks from the meeting after registration tax is paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to record changes in registered particulars exposes the company to administrative fines (the amount of which is set by the Commercial Act) and continuation of an incorrect registry may preclude claims against transferees, trigger loss of limited liability against the counterparty in exceptional cases, or lead to a court order to appoint an inspector/manager.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa is compulsorily audited by an independent certified public accountant if (i) it is a listed SPAC or has made a filing for listing; or (ii) its total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are at least KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx. USD 9.2 million at KRW 1,300/USD). Korean law does not impose a separate turnover or head-count threshold for mandatory external audit; however, a company that controls a listed special purpose acquisition company or is itself consolidated by a listed group must keep K-IFRS consolidated statements audited. The thresholds for audit-review engagements apply to companies with assets between KRW 5 billion and KRW 12 billion only when the company elects a review instead of a full audit under the asset-based small-company exemption, but listed SPACs remain always subject to a full statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Listed SPAC and entities subject to mandatory external audit: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board). Non-listed small and medium-size Yuhan Hoesa entities may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for Non-Public Entities (K-GAAP / SME Accounting Standards) unless parent consolidation requires K-IFRS. The SPAC's trust/escrow assets, refund liabilities, and merger-related contingent warrants must be recognized under K-IFRS 1110 (Consolidated Financial Statements), K-IFRS 1109 (Financial Instruments), and K-IFRS 3 (Business Combinations).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no separate UBO annual return to a Korean central registry for a private Yuhan Hoesa. For capital market instruments, a person holding 5% or more of the SPAC's issued shares must report a material-holdings statement to the FSS and KRX within 5 business days after crossing the threshold, and any subsequent change of 1% or more must be reported within 5 business days. Beneficial ownership for AML/CFT purposes is collected and verified at onboarding and on a risk-sensitive ongoing basis by the Korean financial institution and registered agent under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (STS obligations). The annual business report must set forth major shareholders. A share or membership interest transfer in the Yuhan Hoesa becomes effective against the company only upon entry in the Register of Members; the manager is obliged to reflect the transfer in the commercial register documents within 30 days if the transfer changes a registered person detail.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Register of Members of Yuhan Hoesa)
Register of Directors and Management Members (Directors/Executive Managers Register)
Register of Charges and Security Interests over Movables, Receivables, and Membership Interests
Minute Book of Members' and Managers' Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - USD 45,000 per year for a compliant Korean SPAC with trust and escrow arrangements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax top marginal rate plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a combined top effective rate of 26.4%; progressive brackets are 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No SPAC-specific exemption is available. General incentives include venture and SME preferential corporate tax rates, free economic zone and foreign investment zone corporate tax holidays, R&D and national strategic technology tax credits, and temporary investment tax incentives. A Yuhan Hoesa SPAC remains fully taxable on trust account interest, sponsor compensation income, and gains on acquisition-related arrangements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: National: Corporation Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (Corporate Tax Return Form 4 for a domestic corporation) filed through the NTS HomeTax electronic portal; Local: Local Income Tax Return filed together with the national return for the relevant local government.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return with semi-annual estimated corporate tax payments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year SPAC, the deadline is March 31 of the following year; non-calendar fiscal years are due by the end of the third month after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identity and SPAC Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name (Yuhan Hoesa), business registration number, head office address, fiscal year, industry code ISIC 6499, number of shares and shareholders, and SPAC registration details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all non-resident shareholders and attach their country of residence. Do not conflate founder and sponsor shares with public trust shares. Disclose any non-resident director or manager; if foreign shareholders are treaty-resident, enter the treaty country and beneficial ownership status for later withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Income Statement and Gross Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross income including interest income from trust accounts holding IPO proceeds, management and administration fees, break-up fees, compensation from target acquisition agreements, and any other ordinary income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gross trust interest must be separately shown; it is taxable to the Korean SPAC at the entity level. Interest and fees paid to non-residents must not be netted against SPAC revenue, and any such payments must be cross-referenced to Box 6 for withholding tax declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Accounting-to-Tax Reconciliation and Taxable Income Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add non-deductible expenses such as surplus entertainment expenses, penalties, fines, bribes, sponsorship amounts over statutory limits, and unrealized valuation losses; deduct tax-exempt income, prior-year loss carryforwards, and allowable reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to non-resident related parties, including advisory, due diligence, and sponsor fees, are deductible only if arm's length, documented, and supported by valid withholding and DTA filings; otherwise add them back to taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Loss Carryforward and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter deductible losses from prior years within the statutory carryforward period, foreign tax credits, R&D tax credits, and other special tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean SPAC can use its own carried-forward losses to reduce corporate tax, but this does not reduce the effective 22% non-resident dividend withholding tax. Do not allocate losses to non-resident investors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Taxable Base and Corporate Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply progressive corporate tax rates to taxable income, compute national corporate income tax, add the 10% local income tax surtax, and subtract interim paid taxes and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The statutory entity-level tax is separate from non-resident shareholder withholding tax. Attach a reconciliation showing all trust distributions and confirm that non-resident shareholders' treaty eligibility is not improperly embedded in the entity-level tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Non-Resident Withholding and DTA Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, or other payments made to non-residents; withholding tax at statutory or treaty-reduced rates; DTA relief details; and withholding tax payment records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident payee provide: name, country of residence, Tax Residency Certificate number, beneficial ownership statement, treaty article, applicable rate (for example 10% or 15% on dividends and 10% on interest or royalties under many Korean DTAs), and the monthly withholding tax due date of the 10th day of the following month.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachment showing total amounts of cross-border related-party transactions, pricing methods, comparability adjustments, and transfer pricing documentation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A SPAC with foreign sponsor parties must disclose any compensation paid to the sponsor, transaction services, management fees, loans, or expense reimbursements. Use arm's length methods and attach Master File and Local File documentation if statutory thresholds are met; late submission triggers penalty and adjustment risk.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or under-report attracts a non-filing penalty of 20% of the tax due; a false or incomplete return attracts a penalty of 10% of the understated tax; daily overdue surcharge on unpaid national tax applies under the National Tax Basic Act at approximately 0.03% per day, with a matching local income tax surcharge. Fraudulent returns can trigger criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to twice the evaded tax, plus personal liability of directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% effective rate for non-resident shareholders, composed of 20% national dividend withholding tax plus 10% local income tax surtax, unless reduced by an applicable DTA; general DTA dividend rates are 10% to 15%, with lower rates of 0% to 5% for substantial corporate shareholdings depending on the treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident payee must provide the Korean withholding payer with a current Tax Residency Certificate, evidence of beneficial ownership, and, for reduced dividend rates, proof of shareholding percentage and the corresponding holding period. The payer applies the treaty rate at the time of payment and must submit the application for tax treaty exemption or reduction, including the applicable NTS Form, with the monthly withholding tax return through HomeTax by the 10th day of the following month. Continuous retention of treaty documentation for at least five years is mandatory; backup withholding is required if documentation is incomplete.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory combined rate for interest and royalties paid to non-residents is 22%, being 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax. Many Korean bilateral treaties reduce interest and royalty withholding to 10%; some treaties provide 0% for certain government-approved interest or 10% to 15% for industrial royalties. The same TRC and beneficial ownership protocol applies; royalties from Korean-sourced intellectual property and interest from Korean-sourced debt paid by a Yuhan Hoesa are subject to Korean withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Annual cross-border related-party transactions must be reported on the corporate tax return when the amount exceeds KRW 100 million for a transaction category; mandatory Local File documentation is required when intercompany transactions exceed KRW 50 billion; Master File is required when Korean consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country Report applies to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of KRW 100 billion or more under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs and its Enforcement Decree.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Republic of Korea does not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but Korean tax authorities apply beneficial ownership tests, place of effective management analysis, Korean GAAR, and OECD core income-generating activities or CIGA principles. A SPAC should maintain substantive local governance in Korea, including Korean board meetings, minutes, general meeting records, bank and trust accounts, manager residence, and real decision-making, to avoid foreign residence recharacterization and to sustain treaty protection for dividends, interest, and royalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting trust interest or sponsor compensation from the corporate tax return, fabricating SPAC expenses, using false invoices for due diligence or listing costs, or destroying and tampering with accounting records to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, a violation is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine not exceeding twice the evaded tax; administrative penalties include a 20% non-filing penalty, a 10% under-reporting penalty, and daily overdue surcharge on unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A representative or active director who knowingly causes the false return may be personally liable under Article 401 of the Korean Commercial Act to the company and third parties; the court may order asset restitution, and the tax authority may impose a travel ban or immigration blacklisting until liabilities are paid; criminal conviction can result in imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Unjustified Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into sham or non-arm's length agreements with a foreign sponsor, offshore affiliate, or shell partner, overpaying for advisory, guarantee, or licensing fees, shifting Korean-source profit into a no-tax jurisdiction, or mischaracterizing sponsor economic contributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 4 and 11 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the National Tax Service may reallocate income and impose corresponding income adjustments, with under-reporting penalties of 10% of the additional tax assessed under the National Tax Basic Act and late payment surcharge interest; failure to produce required transfer pricing documentation triggers separate statutory per-document penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve false transfer pricing documentation or intentionally erase intercompany transactions face joint and several compensation liability under Commercial Act Article 401; if documentary fraud is used to evade tax, the directors are subject to criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and travel bans as a collection enforcement measure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Abuse of SPAC Trust Assets Through Concealed Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Yuhan Hoesa SPAC as a shell to collect public IPO proceeds, commingling investor trust money with sponsor operating accounts, concealing non-resident beneficial owners, or undertaking an acquisition for money laundering or foreign exchange evasion despite the SPAC's statutory investment obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Capital Markets Act and the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment are punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years, fines up to KRW 100 million, confiscation of criminal proceeds, and violations of the Real Name Financial Transaction and Guarantee Act can separately generate criminal fines and revocation of the SPAC listing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may have the corporate veil pierced under Korean Supreme Court alter-ego principles when trust assets are treated as personal assets; they are subject to civil liability under Commercial Act Articles 399 and 401, asset freeze orders, Korean immigration blacklisting, and criminal imprisonment terms of up to 5 years for concealment of criminal proceeds.
